name: Cipla Ltd.
business_summary: Mumbai-based branded and generic pharma and API maker. Roughly 45% of sales is India (the 'One India' prescription, trade-generic and consumer-health franchise, strong in respiratory), ~30% US (respiratory inhalers such as generic Advair/Albuterol, gRevlimid, peptides such as lanreotide, complex generics), ~13% South Africa/Africa (SAGA), remainder emerging markets and Europe (mix from model knowledge, to be verified). Q2 FY27 sales Rs 7,404 cr (-2.4% YoY), EBITDA Rs 1,388 cr (18.7%), PAT Rs 852-878 cr (-35% YoY) as gRevlimid fades and costs rise; R&D Rs 423 cr. Net-cash, TTM sales Rs 28,139 cr, mcap Rs 1.13 lakh cr (P/E 36).

revenue_mix.segment: India (One India: Rx, trade generics, consumer health)
revenue_mix.geography: India; record Q2 per management, share = model knowledge

revenue_mix.segment: North America (inhalers, gRevlimid, peptides, complex generics)
South Africa, Africa and emerging markets

exposures.mechanism: US ~30% of sales (~Rs 2,200 cr/qtr); generics base ex-gRevlimid/gAdvair is ~60% of US. +5pp price erosion on that base = -3% US sales = -0.9% group sales; at 18.7% OPM and ~100% drop-through = -4.8% EBITDA; EV/MCap 0.95, persistence 0.5 (erosion compounds for ~1-2 yrs) -> -2.3; plus faster gRevlimid/gAdvair competition risk (Q2 US sales weak, operating margin down from 25% to 19%) -> -3.5. No empirical series for this factor.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 net profit -35% on US weakness; Reuters headline 'misses profit view on US weakness' (2026-10-27)

exposures.mechanism: US imposed 100% tariff on branded/patented pharma from 2026-09-29 with India and 19 other jurisdictions exempted on speciality drugs; generics have been outside the Section 232 action so far (reports 2026-09-29, Business Standard/Firstpost). Cipla US sales are mostly generics made in India (~30% of sales). Probability of a generic tariff within 12m ~10%; if imposed, US margin hit ~50% absorbed -> EBITDA -12% -> equity -10%; +10pp SSU-scaled and probability-weighted -> -0.5 per +10pp. Empirical not significant.

evidence.note: US exempts select Indian specialty drugs from 100% pharma tariff (Open Magazine, Firstpost, Business Standard 2026-09-29)

exposures.mechanism: Large US-supply sites (Goa, Indore, Patalganga) plus inhaler lines; management cited supply issues in Q2 yet retained US$1 bn target (BusinessLine 2026-10-27), implying exposure to supply/inspection slippage. One OAI/warning letter at a core site: ~15% of US revenue at risk for 6-12 months = -1.5% group sales -> EBITDA -8%, +multiple derating; prob 20%/yr x -12% equity + base-level noise -> -2.0 per 'stricter' unit. Also the Oct-2026 FDA cancellation of a wholesale licence of a Cipla entity (Indian Express 2026-10-02; this is a state FDA matter, detail unverified).

evidence.note: Indian Express: FDA cancels wholesale drug sales licence of Cipla Pharma & Life Sciences (state regulator, impact unclear)

exposures.mechanism: USD-linked revenue ~38% of sales (US 30% + other USD/EM 8%), imported inputs ~10% of sales -> net 28% x 3% = +0.84% of sales; at 17-19% OPM = +4.7% EBITDA; ~40% hedged near term -> +2.8%; EV/MCap 0.95, persistence 0.5 -> +1.3 (rounded +1.4 incl. ZAR/EM translation). Empirical +0.83 (t=0.8) same sign, lower; kept above empirical because of hedging uncertainty.

evidence.note: Cipla Q2 FY27: US sales in line, India record, margin compression (CNBC TV18 2026-10-27)

exposures.mechanism: India ~45% of sales and mostly chronic/acute branded Rx plus consumer health; Rx volume growth is weakly tied to discretionary spend. +5pp urban consumption growth lifts consumer health and acute segment by ~1.5pp of India sales = +0.7% group sales, ~50% drop-through at 40% gross incremental margin -> EBITDA +2.4%; EV/MCap 0.95, persistence 0.5 -> +1.1.

evidence.note: Moneycontrol 2026-10-27: Cipla leans on US respiratory launches and India momentum for H2; One India revenue at record

exposures.mechanism: Cipla buys a share of APIs/intermediates from China (model knowledge ~15-20% of RM). +15% Chinese export price cuts lower API cost ~3% of RM = RM is ~30% of costs -> -0.9% costs ~ +4% EBITDA at 17% OPM if not competed away; ~50% retained, EV/MCap 0.95, persistence 0.3 -> +0.6; rounded +0.8. Sign uncertain because cheap APIs also intensify generic competition.

evidence.note: Margin 18.7% (Kalkine Media 2026-10-30) well below FY25 26%: input and mix costs matter

exposures.mechanism: Almost debt-free (interest Rs 17 cr/qtr); only a valuation-multiple channel: +25bp repo -> higher discount rate on a 36x P/E defensive; ~-0.6% via duration. Empirical not significant (US 10y +0.51 t=1.2, wrong direction for duration).

evidence.note: Interest Rs 17 cr per quarter against EBITDA Rs 1,388 cr (screener.in Sep 2026)

exposures.mechanism: Management flagged Middle East tensions adding cost (Moneycontrol 2026-10-27): freight, packaging, solvent costs, and Gulf/Africa shipping lanes (SAGA/EM ~18% of sales). Escalation unit: freight and chemicals +10% on ~8% of costs = +0.8% cost -> EBITDA -4%; persistence 0.25, EV/MCap 0.95 -> -1.0. Brent has +15% in 3m but empirical Brent sensitivity is positive (+0.44, t=1.1), i.e. not a negative market signal.

evidence.note: Moneycontrol: 'Middle East tensions add cost...' in Cipla Q2 commentary

exposures.mechanism: India prescription market grows ~8-9% nominal regardless; +1pp real GDP adds ~0.3pp to India pharma volumes; 45% of sales x 0.3% = +0.14% sales, ~+0.7% EBITDA, persistence 1.0 on structural trend share -> +0.5; rounded +0.8 to include multiple effect.

evidence.note: Record One India revenue in Q2 FY27 (TradingView 2026-10-27)

exposures.mechanism: FIIs hold 20.2% (down from 22.6% in Mar 2026) while DIIs rose to 34.6%; stock beta 0.65. +US$5bn FPI quarterly inflow lifts large-caps ~3% -> beta-scaled and defensive tilt gives +0.6 extra.
